function.name: create_file
function.description: This is a tool for creating a new file in the workspace. The file will be created with the specified content. The directory will be created if it does not already exist. Never use this tool to edit a file that already exists.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to create.

content.description: The content to write to the file.

function.name: fetch_webpage
function.description: Fetches the main content from a web page. This tool is useful for summarizing or analyzing the content of a webpage. You should use this tool when you think the user is looking for information from a specific webpage.

urls.description: An array of URLs to fetch content from.

query.description: The query to search for in the web page's content. This should be a clear and concise description of the content you want to find.

function.name: search_patents
function.description: Executes an EPO OPS CQL patent search for EP/WO patents; returns summaries (title, applicant, publication date, abstract). Preferred when the query targets European or international (WO) patents — not US patents (for those, use build_uspto_query then patent_api_request; see uspto_api_guide for advanced options). Use after build_patent_query to run the generated CQL. Input: query (CQL string, e.g. 'pa=Tesla and ic=H01M and pd>=2022'); range ('1-25', '26-50' for pagination); countries (e.g. 'EP,WO' to restrict to fulltext-available patents). No wildcards on ic/cpc fields; max 100 results per request.

query.description: CQL query string (preferably from build_patent_query tool). Examples: 'pa=Pfizer* AND ic=A61K AND ti=cancer', 'pa=Vestas* AND ic=F03D AND ti="wind turbine"'. IMPORTANT: No wildcards on ic/cpc fields.

range.description: Result range in format 'start-end', e.g., '1-25', '26-50'. Max 100 results per request. Use pagination for more results.

countries.description: Filter by country codes (optional). Use 'EP,WO' to get only European/WIPO patents with fulltext available. Default: all countries.

function.name: analyze_claim
function.description: Analyze user's invention/claim to extract searchable elements. USE WHEN: User describes THEIR OWN invention, claim, or idea and wants prior art analysis or patentability assessment. TRIGGER PHRASES: 'my invention', 'my idea', 'analyze my claim', 'is my idea patentable', 'prior art for my concept'. Returns: keywords, synonyms, IPC codes, suggested CQL queries, claim element breakdown. WORKFLOW: After analysis, use suggested queries with search_patents, then compare_claims to assess overlaps.

claimText.description: The patent claim or invention description to analyze. Can be a formal claim or informal description of the invention.

focus.description: What to extract: 'search' returns keywords, synonyms, IPC codes and suggested queries only; 'elements' returns the claim element breakdown only; 'full' (default) returns both.

function.name: compare_claims
function.description: Compare a user's patent claim against one or more existing patents to identify overlaps and differences. WORKFLOW: (1) First use analyze_claim to understand the user's claim, (2) Use search_patents to find potentially relevant patents, (3) Then use THIS tool to compare the user's claim against specific patent numbers. Fetches the actual claims of each cited patent from EPO OPS and returns them alongside the user's claim with an analysis rubric — YOU then perform the element-by-element comparison: relevance (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), overlapping elements, missing elements (potential novelty), key differences, and a 102/103 risk summary. NOTE: EPO OPS full text covers mainly EP/WO publications; for US patents whose claims are unavailable, fetch them via patent_api_request (POST /patent-search-uspto/search). Useful for patentability assessment, freedom-to-operate analysis, and prior art evaluation.

userClaim.description: The user's patent claim or invention description to compare

patentNumbers.description: Array of patent publication numbers to compare against (e.g., ['US-7654321-B2', 'EP-1234567-A1'])

function.name: patent_analytics_viz
function.description: PRIORITY TOOL FOR ANALYTICS: Use this tool when users ask about patent trends, landscapes, market analysis, or competitive intelligence. Runs a full-corpus aggregation over the backend patent corpus (a quarterly-refreshed slice of the Google Patents corpus) and returns ready-made markdown TABLES: filing trend by publication year, top assignees, country breakdown, and top CPC sections (each capped at top 20). Present the tables directly — they are the deliverable; you do NOT need to write Python or generate charts. TRIGGER KEYWORDS: 'trends', 'chart', 'dashboard', 'landscape', 'top companies', 'market analysis', 'geographic', 'filing trends', 'competitive analysis', 'patent portfolio'. DO NOT use build_patent_query for analytics - use THIS tool directly. Provide at least one criterion. PREFERRED: Use 'keywords' array for individual terms (preserves short terms like 'AI', '5G'), use 'phrases' for exact matches like 'machine learning'.

keywords.description: PREFERRED: Individual keywords with OR logic. Each keyword is searched independently. Preserves short terms like 'AI', '5G', 'ML'. Example: ['AI', 'healthcare', '5G']

phrases.description: Exact phrase matches. Use for multi-word terms that must appear together. Example: ['machine learning', 'deep learning', 'neural network']

assignee.description: Filter by harmonized assignee name (substring match, e.g. 'Tesla', 'Toyota', 'Apple')

cpc.description: Filter by CPC classification codes (prefix match). Example: ['G06N', 'A61B', 'H04L']

ipc.description: Filter by IPC classification codes (prefix match). Example: ['G06F', 'H01M']

dateFrom.description: Publication-date lower bound in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2020-01-01')

dateTo.description: Publication-date upper bound in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., '2024-12-31')

function.name: get_patent_summary
function.description: DEFAULT entry point for a single-patent OVERVIEW question. One call returns a compound snapshot from multiple backend sources: bibliographic data (title, applicants, inventors, dates, IPC/CPC), the abstract, the latest legal-status events, patent-family size, and the estimated term — collapsing what used to take 3-4 separate round-trips. USE WHEN the user asks about ONE known patent in general terms: 'tell me about patent X', 'what is US10123456 about', 'give me an overview/summary of EP1234567', 'summarize this patent'. INPUT: a publication number (e.g. 'EP1234567', 'US10123456'; hyphens optional). Does NOT return full claims or description text — for those use get_patent_details; for drawings use get_patent_figures; for a dedicated expiry estimate use get_patent_term.

function.name: get_patent_term
function.description: Estimate a patent's TERM / EXPIRY. Returns the filing date, the estimated base expiry date (20 years from filing), the basis, and a disclaimer covering the adjustments the base estimate does NOT include (PTA/PTE, SPCs, terminal disclaimers, annuity lapses). USE WHEN the user asks about a patent's lifespan: 'when does US10123456 expire', 'patent term', 'expiration date', 'is EP1234567 still in force', 'how long until this patent expires'. INPUT: a publication number (hyphens optional). This is a base estimate, not the enforceable expiry — for lapse/adjustment data point the user to get_patent_summary (legal-status events).

function.name: compare_patents
function.description: Data-grounded, side-by-side comparison of 2 to 10 PUBLISHED patent documents. Fetches each document's bibliographic record from the backend and renders an attribute-by-patent comparison table (title, applicants, inventors, filing/publication/priority dates, IPC/CPC) plus bounded abstracts, so YOU can read off the similarities and differences. USE WHEN the user wants to compare EXISTING patents to each other: 'compare patents US10123456 and EP1234567', 'what's the difference between these patents', 'how do these two patents relate'. INPUT: an array of 2-10 publication numbers. IMPORTANT — this is DOCUMENT-to-DOCUMENT: do NOT use it for a user's own DRAFTED claim text against references (that is compare_claims, which builds an element-by-element claim chart). For a single patent use get_patent_summary or get_patent_details.

patentNumbers.description: Array of 2-10 published patent publication numbers to compare (e.g., ['US10123456', 'EP1234567', 'WO2020123456']; hyphens optional).

function.name: get_patent_details
function.description: Retrieve patent details from EPO OPS: bibliographic data (title, abstract, applicants, inventors, dates, IPC/CPC classifications) plus full CLAIMS and DESCRIPTION where published. Use this tool AFTER search_patents when users need: (1) full claims text for infringement/validity analysis, (2) detailed description for technical understanding, (3) complete patent document analysis. WORKFLOW: First use build_patent_query + search_patents to find relevant patents, then use THIS tool to get full text for specific patents of interest. FORMAT: Pass the publication number in EPO epodoc format without hyphens (US7654321B2, EP1234567A1, WO2020123456A1); hyphenated input is normalized automatically. NOTE: OPS full text covers mainly EP/WO publications — biblio and abstract resolve for all jurisdictions, and for US full text the output points you to the USPTO fallback (patent_api_request).

function.name: get_patent_figures
function.description: Retrieve patent figure/drawing IMAGES and return them as inline PNG images you can SEE and analyze. USE WHEN: the user asks to see, show, view, or analyze the figures, drawings, or images of a specific patent. The backend fetches the drawings from EPO and rasterizes them to PNG, so they render directly in chat. INPUT: a patent publication number (e.g. 'EP1234567', 'US10000000B2'; hyphens optional). By default returns the actual DRAWING pages (EPO scans put cover/biblio/description pages first, so they are skipped automatically); pass 'pages' (e.g. '1,2,3') to override and fetch specific pages. Do NOT use this for full claims/description text — use get_patent_details for text.

pages.description: Optional comma-separated page numbers to fetch, e.g. '1,2,3' (max 20). If omitted, returns the first several figure pages.

function.name: get_legal_status
function.description: PRIMARY tool for the LEGAL STATUS of a known patent: returns the INPADOC legal-status event history (grants, lapses, withdrawals, renewal-fee payments, oppositions) from EPO OPS as a per-jurisdiction chronological table, from which in-force vs. lapsed/expired is read. Use whenever the user asks whether a patent is still in force / valid / active, whether it has lapsed or expired, about maintenance/renewal fees, or whether it was opposed. Prefer this over ops_api_guide + patent_api_request legal endpoints for standard legal-status lookups; use the raw path only for advanced cases the typed tool doesn't cover. Input: publicationNumber in epodoc format (e.g. 'EP1000000', 'US10000000B2'; hyphens normalized). For the patent family across jurisdictions use get_patent_family; for EP register prosecution events use get_register_events.

function.name: get_patent_family
function.description: PRIMARY tool for the PATENT FAMILY of a known patent: returns the INPADOC family members (equivalents/counterparts filed in other jurisdictions) from EPO OPS as a table of country, publication number and kind code. Use whenever the user asks about a patent's family, INPADOC family, foreign equivalents/counterparts, or where a patent was also filed or granted in other countries. Prefer this over ops_api_guide + patent_api_request family endpoints for standard family lookups; use the raw path only for advanced cases the typed tool doesn't cover. Input: publicationNumber in epodoc format (e.g. 'EP1000000', 'US10000000B2'; hyphens normalized). For the legal status of a member use get_legal_status; for EP register prosecution events use get_register_events.

function.name: get_register_events
function.description: PRIMARY tool for the EP REGISTER prosecution events of a known patent: returns the EPO Register event history (oppositions, transfers of rights, amendments, lapses, procedural steps) as a chronological table. Use whenever the user asks about a patent's register events, opposition proceedings, transfers or assignments of rights, or EP prosecution/procedural history. EP applications/patents only. Prefer this over ops_api_guide + patent_api_request register endpoints for standard register lookups; use the raw path only for advanced cases the typed tool doesn't cover. Input: publicationNumber in epodoc format (e.g. 'EP1000000'; hyphens normalized). For INPADOC legal-status events across all jurisdictions use get_legal_status; for the patent family use get_patent_family.

publicationNumber.description: EP patent publication number, e.g. 'EP1000000', 'EP1234567B1' (hyphens optional).

function.name: read_pdf
function.description: Extract text content from a local PDF file. Use this tool when users reference PDF documents (patent PDFs, research papers, technical documents) and need to analyze their content. Reads all pages by default, a single page via 'pageNumber', or a range via 'startPage'/'endPage'. Returns extracted text plus metadata (title, author, page count). The PDF must be a local file accessible from the workspace.

filePath.description: The absolute path of the PDF file to read.

startPage.description: Optional: the 1-based page number to start reading from. If omitted, reads from page 1.

endPage.description: Optional: the 1-based page number to stop reading at (inclusive). If omitted, reads to the last page.

pageNumber.description: Optional: read only this specific page number (1-based). Takes precedence over startPage/endPage.

function.name: search_citations
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL for backward citation search: finds prior-art references cited by examiners against a USPTO application (X = novelty-destroying/102, Y = obviousness/103, A = background). Use whenever the user asks about citations against an application, examiner prior art, or X/Y/A rejection references. Prefer this over citation_api_guide + patent_api_request for standard citation lookups — use citation_api_guide only for date-range filtering or citation statistics. Input: applicationNumber (numeric string, no slashes — normalize '16/000,001' to '16000001'); category ('X'/'Y'/'A', omit for all); examinerOnly (boolean); size (default 100).

applicationNumber.description: USPTO application number, numeric only, no slashes or commas. If the user writes '16/000,001' or '16,000,001', normalize to '16000001'.

category.description: Optional filter. X = novelty-destroying (35 USC 102), Y = obviousness (35 USC 103), A = background. Omit to return all categories.

examinerOnly.description: Optional. If true, return only examiner-cited references (exclude applicant-cited). Default: false.

size.description: Optional. Maximum number of citations to return. Default: 100.

function.name: search_forward_citations
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL for forward citation impact analysis: finds patents that CITE a given document, measuring its influence as prior art. Use when asked 'who cites this patent', 'forward citations', 'impact analysis', or 'how influential is X'. Distinct from search_citations (which finds prior art cited against an application): this tool takes a document being cited and returns the citing patents. Prefer this over citation_api_guide + patent_api_request for standard forward lookups. Input: citedDocument (patent/publication number in any standard format, e.g. 'US 20150284881 A1' or 'EP 1234567 A1'); category ('X'/'Y'/'A', omit for all); examinerOnly (boolean); size (default 100).

citedDocument.description: The document being cited - patent or publication number. Accepted formats: 'US 20150284881 A1', 'US-10000001-B2', 'EP 1234567 A1', 'WO 2020123456 A1'. Pass as the user provided it - do not aggressively normalize.

category.description: Optional filter. X = novelty-destroying (35 USC 102), Y = obviousness (35 USC 103), A = background. Omit for all categories. X-rated forward citations indicate the document is strong prior art.

examinerOnly.description: Optional. If true, return only examiner-cited references (more significant than applicant-cited). Default: false.

size.description: Optional. Maximum number of citing patents to return. Default: 100.

function.name: get_continuity
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL for the USPTO parent/child continuity chain of a US application: the divisionals, continuations, and continuations-in-part that make up a patent family, with each relationship (CON/DIV/CIP/PRO), filing date, patent number, and status. Use whenever the user asks about continuity, the parent application, child/divisional/continuation applications, the priority chain, or double patenting (the parent it runs over). This returns the applicant's OWN related filings — NOT prior art. Do NOT confuse with search_citations (examiner-cited prior art X/Y/A) or get_prosecution_timeline (legal-event chronology). Prefer this over the raw uspto_api_guide continuity path for standard continuity lookups. Input: applicationNumber (numeric string, no slashes — normalize '16/123,456' to '16123456').

applicationNumber.description: USPTO application number, numeric only, no slashes or commas. If the user writes '16/123,456', normalize to '16123456'.

function.name: get_prosecution_timeline
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL for a chronological prosecution / legal-status timeline of a patent: merges EP Register events and INPADOC legal-status events (filing, search report, grant, oppositions, assignments, renewals/maintenance-fee payments, lapse) into one dated chronology. Use whenever the user asks about the prosecution history, the file wrapper / legal-event timeline, what happened during prosecution, grant/opposition/lapse history, or maintenance status over time. Most complete for EP/WO; for US patents it surfaces the INPADOC legal events (assignment, grant, maintenance fees). Do NOT confuse with search_citations (examiner-cited prior art X/Y/A) or get_continuity (parent/child application chain). Input: publicationNumber — a PUBLICATION number (US10123456, EP1000000, WO2020123456; hyphens optional), NOT an application number.

function.name: citation_api_guide
function.description: Documentation for the USPTO Citation Search API. DEFER TO TYPED TOOLS for the common cases: use search_citations for prior art cited AGAINST an application (input: applicationNumber), use search_forward_citations for patents that CITE a given document (input: citedDocument, impact analysis). Use THIS guide tool ONLY for advanced cases not covered by either typed tool: (1) citation statistics aggregations (/stats endpoint), (2) novelty-only convenience endpoint, (3) date-range filtering, (4) general API exploration. X = novelty-destroying (102), Y = obviousness (103), A = background. Available actions: 'list', 'endpoint' (search, forward, stats, novelty), 'workflow' (prior-art-analysis, impact-analysis, claim-analysis), 'full'. After getting docs, call the endpoint via patent_api_request.

action.description: Action type: 'list' for compact endpoint list, 'endpoint' for specific endpoint docs, 'workflow' for task guides, 'full' for complete docs

endpoint.description: Endpoint name when action='endpoint'. Options: search, forward, stats, novelty

workflow.description: Workflow name when action='workflow'. Options: prior-art-analysis, impact-analysis, claim-analysis

function.name: build_patent_query
function.description: Translates a natural-language invention or topic description into an EPO CQL query for EP/WO prior-art search. Use for prior-art research, patentability assessment, and EP/WO patent landscape searches — prefer this over manual CQL when the search involves technical keywords, IPC/CPC codes, or applicant names. Call ONCE per search intent, then immediately call search_patents with the returned CQL. For US patent searches use build_uspto_query instead. Input: description (free text of the invention or topic); focus ('broad'/'precise'/'comprehensive'). EPO CQL limits: no wildcards on ic/cpc fields, max ~10 terms per query.

description.description: Natural language description of what patents to search for. Examples: 'Pfizer patents about cancer treatment', 'wind turbine patents from Vestas or Siemens', 'Tesla battery technology patents', 'agricultural drone patents', 'Boeing aircraft wing designs'

focus.description: Search focus: 'broad' for exploratory searches, 'precise' for specific known-item searches, 'comprehensive' for thorough research. Default: comprehensive

function.name: build_uspto_query
function.description: Translates a natural-language description into a USPTO Open Data Portal (ODP) Lucene search body for US patent searches. Use before every USPTO search — it knows the current ODP field names and avoids the legacy PatentsView parameters (query/assignee/cpcCode/dateRange no longer exist). Prefer this over manual ODP body construction for any query beyond a trivial single keyword. For EP/WO patents use build_patent_query instead. Input: description (free text); focus ('broad'/'precise'/'comprehensive'). Call ONCE per intent, then use the result with uspto_api_guide.

description.description: Natural language description of US patents to search for. Examples: 'Google AI patents from 2023', 'Tesla battery technology patents', 'Apple face recognition patents'

focus.description: Search focus: 'broad' for exploratory, 'precise' for specific, 'comprehensive' for thorough. Default: comprehensive

function.name: patent_api_request
function.description: Make an authenticated request to the Patent AI backend and get the JSON result directly. Use this for ANY backend endpoint shown by the *_api_guide tools (OPS, USPTO, citation, legal) — supply the `path` (e.g. /ops/biblio?doc=EP1234566), optional `method` (GET default, or POST), and optional `body` (a JSON string for POST). Prefer this over running curl in the terminal: it authenticates automatically and returns structured results. Do NOT put the backend host or /v1 in the path.

path.description: Relative path to the backend endpoint, e.g. "/ops/biblio?doc=EP1234566" or "/patent-search-uspto". Do NOT include the host or /v1 prefix.

method.description: HTTP method. Defaults to GET. Use POST when the endpoint expects a request body.

body.description: JSON-serialised request body for POST requests. Must be valid JSON, e.g. '{"q":"battery","filters":{}}'. Omit or leave empty for GET requests.

function.name: ops_api_guide
function.description: Get documentation for EPO OPS (Open Patent Services) API endpoints. Use this tool FIRST to learn available endpoints and request shapes, then call them with the patent_api_request tool (authenticated, no terminal needed). Available actions: 'list' (compact endpoint list), 'endpoint' (detailed docs for specific endpoint), 'workflow' (step-by-step guides for common tasks like prior-art-search, citation-analysis, competitor-analysis), 'full' (complete documentation). After getting docs, call the endpoint via patent_api_request; respect the documented rate limits between sequential calls.

action.description: Action type: 'list' for compact endpoint list, 'endpoint' for specific endpoint docs, 'workflow' for task guides, 'full' for complete docs

endpoint.description: Endpoint name when action='endpoint'. Options: search, biblio, biblio-bulk, abstract, fulltext, fulltext-claims, fulltext-description, fulltext-availability, family, legal, citations, figures, figures-download, equivalents, number-service, family-biblio, family-legal, register-biblio, register-events, register-procedural, register-upp

workflow.description: Workflow name when action='workflow'. Options: prior-art-search, citation-analysis, competitor-analysis, freedom-to-operate

function.name: uspto_api_guide
function.description: Get documentation for the USPTO Open Data Portal (ODP) API endpoints — the single source of truth for the current request shapes (the API migrated from PatentsView; legacy parameters no longer exist). Use this tool FIRST to learn available endpoints, then call them with the patent_api_request tool (authenticated, no terminal needed). Available actions: 'list' (compact endpoint list), 'endpoint' (detailed docs for specific endpoint like 'search' or 'grants'), 'workflow' (step-by-step guides for basic-search, assignee-search, citation-analysis, date-filtered-search), 'full' (complete documentation). After getting docs, call the endpoint via patent_api_request.

action.description: Action type: 'list' for compact endpoint list, 'endpoint' for specific endpoint docs, 'workflow' for task guides, 'full' for complete docs

endpoint.description: Endpoint name when action='endpoint'. Options: search, grants, application, continuity

workflow.description: Workflow name when action='workflow'. Options: basic-search, assignee-search, citation-analysis, date-filtered-search

function.name: search_legal
function.description: PRIMARY TOOL for patent law and procedure lookups: searches MPEP (USPTO), EPC, and EPO Guidelines using hybrid semantic + keyword search. Use whenever the user asks about patent law, examination procedure, statutory bases (35 USC, EPC Articles), or wants to look up MPEP sections or EPO Guidelines. Prefer this over legal_search_guide + patent_api_request for standard queries; use legal_search_guide only for advanced cases (custom search modes, similarity thresholds). Input: query (free text, e.g. 'obviousness 103 prima facie Graham factors'); jurisdiction ('USPTO' for MPEP, 'EPO' for EPC/Guidelines, omit for all); comprehensive (true = full section content for quoting, false = matched chunks); limit (default 10).

query.description: Free-text legal search query, minimum 3 characters. Examples: 'obviousness 103 prima facie', 'MPEP 2143 Graham factors', 'EPC Article 54 novelty', 'inventive step problem-solution approach'.

jurisdiction.description: Optional filter. Omit to search across all jurisdictions. Use USPTO for MPEP, EPO for EPC and EPO Guidelines.

comprehensive.description: Optional. If true, returns full section content grouped by document (better for quoting full rules). If false (default), returns matched chunks with similarity scores (better for quick lookup).

limit.description: Optional. Maximum results to return. Default: 10.

function.name: legal_search_guide
function.description: Documentation for the Legal RAG Search API (MPEP, EPC, EPO Guidelines). DEFER TO search_legal for basic legal lookup queries — that typed tool covers the common case (search MPEP/EPC/EPO Guidelines with optional jurisdiction filter and comprehensive mode). Use THIS guide tool ONLY for advanced cases not covered by search_legal: (1) specific source filters (e.g., restrict to MPEP only and exclude EPC), (2) custom search modes (semantic-only or keyword-only instead of hybrid), (3) semantic-weight tuning, (4) similarity threshold tuning, (5) stats and jurisdictions meta endpoints, (6) general API exploration. Available actions: 'list', 'endpoint' (search, stats, jurisdictions), 'workflow' (mpep-lookup, epc-research, cross-jurisdiction), 'full'. After getting docs, call the endpoint via patent_api_request.

action.description: Action type: 'list' for compact endpoint list, 'endpoint' for specific endpoint docs, 'workflow' for task guides, 'full' for complete docs

endpoint.description: Endpoint name when action='endpoint'. Options: search, stats, jurisdictions

workflow.description: Workflow name when action='workflow'. Options: mpep-lookup, epc-research, cross-jurisdiction

function.name: search_academic
function.description: Searches academic research papers (Google Scholar, arXiv, PubMed) for non-patent literature (NPL) prior art. Use for prior-art research when the invention has academic antecedents, or when the user asks for scientific papers, research publications, or NPL references. Complements patent searches — combine with EP/WO search (search_patents) and US search (build_uspto_query + patent_api_request) for comprehensive prior-art coverage. Not a substitute for patent databases — use dedicated patent tools for EP/WO and US patents. Input: query (free text, e.g. 'CRISPR gene editing off-target effects'); sources (['scholar','arxiv','pubmed'], default ['scholar','arxiv']); maxResults (default 10, max 50).

query.description: Search query for academic papers (e.g., 'neural networks image classification', 'CRISPR gene editing')

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 50)

function.name: write_patent_results
function.description: Write patent search results or analysis to a local file. Use this tool when the user asks to save patent search results to a file. This tool does not require GitHub Copilot authentication and works directly with the file system.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the file to write (e.g., '/Users/username/Desktop/patents.md')

content.description: The content to write to the file (markdown, plain text, JSON, etc.). When a 'template' is supplied, this content is placed in the report's results/analysis section.

template.description: Optional report template that wraps 'content' in a professional structure (title block, matter/date fields, standard sections, results area, and a not-legal-advice disclaimer). 'prior-art-report' for prior-art search reports, 'fto-memo' for freedom-to-operate memoranda, 'office-action-scaffold' for office-action responses, 'invalidity-claim-chart' for element-by-element invalidity charts, 'eou-infringement-chart' for element-by-element evidence-of-use/infringement charts, 'patentability-opinion' for novelty and non-obviousness opinions, 'landscape-report' for technology landscape analyses, 'portfolio-due-diligence-memo' for portfolio due-diligence memoranda. Omit for a free-form save of the raw content.

function.name: patent_search_subagent
function.description: Autonomous patent search subagent. Delegates patent and academic literature searching to a specialized subagent that runs in its own context. The subagent searches EPO (via CQL), USPTO, and academic sources (arXiv, Google Scholar) using optimized queries. Use this when you need comprehensive patent research without cluttering the main conversation. The subagent will search multiple databases in parallel and return structured findings including patent numbers, titles, abstracts, and relevance assessments.

query.description: Natural language description of the technology or invention to search for

description.description: Short user-visible description shown while searching

details.description: Detailed instructions for the search including jurisdictions, classification codes, date ranges, or specific aspects to focus on

function.name: vscode_askQuestions
function.description: Present interactive questions to the user via a carousel UI. Use for jurisdiction clarification before patent searches.

questions.description: List of questions to ask the user. Order is preserved.

header.description: Short identifier for the question. Must be unique so answers can be mapped back to the question. Maximum 50 characters.

question.description: The question text to display to the user. Keep it concise, ideally one sentence. Maximum 200 characters.

multiSelect.description: Allow selecting multiple options when options are provided.

allowFreeformInput.description: Allow freeform text answers in addition to option selection. Defaults to true; set to false to restrict to predefined options only.

message.description: Optional markdown message to display below the question text, providing additional context or details.

options.description: Optional list of selectable answers. If omitted, the question is free text.

label.description: Display label and value for the option.

description.description: Optional secondary text shown with the option.

recommended.description: Mark this option as the recommended default.

function.name: run_in_terminal
